sources.quote: As a result, federal agencies can unknowingly execute contract actions, including awarding a new contract, to contractors that have been suspended or debarred.
sources.page_context: eting an exclusion entry for suspended and debarred contractors without entering a unique entity identifier.1 What We Found GSA does not update the exclusion status for suspended and debarred contractors in its eTools, which consist of GSA Advantage!, GSA eLibrary, and GSA eBuy, in a timely manner. As a result, federal agencies can unknowingly execute contract actions, including awarding a new contract, to contractors that have been suspended or debarred. We found several instances where excluded contractors were incorrectly listed on GSA’s eTools and one instance where an agency purchased services off a GSA Multiple Award Schedule contract from an excluded contractor.
